question: If the Sun vanished, when would Earth stop feeling its pull?
answer: Gravity isn't instant: according to Einstein's relativity it travels at the speed of light, 300,000 km/s. Across 150 million km that takes 8 min 20 s, so Earth keeps circling an empty spot until the news arrives.
move: Gravity moves at light speed: even losing the Sun takes 8 min 20 s to reach us.

web.label: A clock counting down, with the Earth circling an empty spot in space. Asks when Earth would stop feeling the Sun's pull if the Sun vanished. A button makes the Sun vanish 8 min 20 s later.

source: Geopop, “Come potremmo sopravvivere se il Sole scomparisse: gli scenari di una Terra senza luce” (YouTube, 2025)
